title: Caldova Superannuation Master Fund Trust Deed — Death benefits & nominations (rules extract)
version: Trust deed consolidated to 1 July 2026 — Part 9 (death benefits)
summary: Plain-English extract of the trust deed rules that govern how Caldova Superannuation Services Pty Ltd, as trustee of the Caldova Superannuation Master Fund, pays a member's benefit when they die: who can receive it, how binding death benefit nominations (BDBNs) are made and when they are valid, non-binding nominations, reversionary pensions, payment to the legal personal representative (estate) and the form of payment. Benefits & Eligibility cite the clause numbers (TD 9.x) when assessing a death benefit claim. The deed sits alongside the SIS Act and SIS Regulations — in particular reg 6.17A for binding nominations.
rules:
TD 9.1 Payment on death — when a member dies the trustee pays the member's benefit (account balance plus any insured death benefit received) as soon as practicable to one or more of the member's dependants and/or the legal personal representative (LPR).
TD 9.2 Dependants — a SIS dependant is the member's spouse (including a de facto partner of any gender), a child of any age (including adopted, step and ex-nuptial children) or a person in an interdependency relationship with the member.
TD 9.3 Binding death benefit nomination — the trustee must pay in line with a valid, in-force BDBN and has no discretion. To be valid the nomination must: be in writing on the Caldova form; be signed and dated by the member in the presence of two witnesses who are each aged 18 or over and not named as a beneficiary in the nomination; include a declaration signed by each witness that the member signed and dated it in their presence; nominate only SIS dependants and/or the LPR; and state clear proportions totalling 100%.
TD 9.4 Lapsing — a Caldova BDBN lapses 3 years after the date it was signed, last confirmed or amended. Caldova does not accept non-lapsing nominations. A member can revoke or replace a BDBN at any time using the same formalities.
TD 9.5 Invalid or partly invalid nomination — if a nomination fails the formalities or has lapsed, or a nominee has died or is no longer a dependant, it is not binding (in whole or for that share) and the trustee decides the distribution, treating the nomination as an indication of the member's wishes.
TD 9.6 Non-binding nomination — guides the trustee but does not bind it.
TD 9.7 Reversionary pension — a pension may be set up at commencement to revert to a reversionary beneficiary (for example a spouse). On death the pension continues to that person; the reversionary nomination takes priority over any BDBN for that pension account.
TD 9.8 Form of payment — a death benefit may be paid as a lump sum, or as a pension to an eligible dependant (a spouse; or a child under 18, under 25 and financially dependent, or with a disability). Death benefits to anyone else, including adult children, must be paid as lump sums and cannot be rolled over.
TD 9.9 Pension accounts — pension payments stop when Caldova is notified of the member's death unless the pension reverts. Investments are redeemed to cash and the benefit paid reflects actual sale proceeds.
limits: The trustee cannot follow a nomination that is invalid — for example only one witness, a witness who is a named beneficiary, missing witness declarations, unsigned or undated — or that has lapsed; it is treated as non-binding. A BDBN cannot direct a benefit straight to someone who is not a SIS dependant (such as a sibling, friend or charity); the member would need to nominate the LPR so the benefit is paid under the will. Payment to the LPR requires a grant of probate or letters of administration. For discretionary distributions the trustee notifies the proposed distribution and allows a 28-day objection period; complaints about death benefit distributions have a 90-day internal dispute resolution timeframe after that period ends, then AFCA.
evidenceRequired: Certified copy of the death certificate
The member's BDBN or other nominations held on file (with lapse date)
Death benefit claim form and certified identity for each claimant
Evidence of relationship (e.g. birth certificates, marriage certificate, evidence of a de facto or interdependency relationship)
Statement of financial dependency from each claimant (needed for the tax treatment and for discretionary decisions)
Grant of probate or letters of administration (only when paying the LPR)
Bank account details in each payee's own name
